runtime.summary:
Read-only review of CARE backend code outside the model definitions (apps/backend), looking at what matters for one PostgreSQL schema per hospital. No repo files were changed.

Main conclusion: once each request is routed to its tenant's schema, the database queries themselves become tenant-scoped. The real leaks are in shared state outside the database. Every schema gets its own BigAutoField sequence starting at 1 (base.py:75). Many Redis cache keys, Redis lock keys, in-process dicts and Celery task arguments are built from those integer PKs or from fixed strings. So hospital A's facility id=1 and hospital B's facility id=1 share one cache entry.

1. Confirmed cross-tenant data or authorisation leaks:
   - model_from_cache (Facility, PatientIdentifierConfig, TagConfig) is keyed by integer PK.
   - FacilityConfig billing tax and discount caches.
   - FacilityFlag caches.
   - Role-permission caches (if roles are per tenant).
   - The PlugConfig list: unauthenticated, with one fixed cache key.
   - The patient-identifier CACHED_CONFIG process dict, which can attach another schema's config PK to a new PatientIdentifier row.
2. Authentication is not bound to a tenant:
   - SimpleJWT access/refresh tokens (no tenant claim), the patient OTP PatientToken (phone number only) and DRF authtoken service-account tokens.
   - is_superuser / is_staff bypass every authorisation check. If User lives in a shared schema, they bypass it in every tenant.
   - UserViewSet lists every user with no scoping.
3. Celery: no task carries tenant context, and the three periodic tasks run once against the default schema. They need to fan out per tenant.
4. Locks: global lock keys (create_patient, create_invoice, sync_permissions_roles) serialise work across all hospitals, and integer-keyed locks clash across tenants.
5. The default cache has no KEY_PREFIX or KEY_FUNCTION. A schema-aware KEY_FUNCTION in settings (outside apps/ code) fixes most cache and lock collisions in one place. It does not cover:
   - RecentViewsManager, which uses a raw Redis client;
   - the in-process patient-identifier CACHED_CONFIG dicts;
   - Celery task arguments.
   Those three need small logged patches, or plugin/infra handling.
6. Audit logs carry no tenant id and log ambiguous integer PKs. AuditLogMiddleware.cleanup() is never called, and per-request state sits on the model class's shared _meta.
7. Design choices are needed on shared vs per-tenant apps:
   - contenttypes, auth, sessions, sites, admin, authtoken;
   - roles/permissions and valuesets;
   - users;
   - government (geo) organisations, which share the Organization table with team and role organisations.
8. Cross-facility features (resource requests, global patient search, PATIENT_GLOBAL_EDIT_ACCESS, the public facility list) become hospital-only under this design. Cross-hospital referral and continuity of care need a separate route (ABDM or a cross-tenant service).
9. File storage uses one bucket per type, with keys "{file_type}/{uuid4+ts}" and no tenant prefix. Names will not collide, but there is no per-tenant IAM, export, erasure or lifecycle. The patient bucket is signed with the FACILITY_S3 credentials. URLs use UUID/slug/username lookups only (no integer IDs in paths).

Evidence for each item is in the findings, as file:line paths relative to /home/ubuntu/AI Projects/IndieHR/apps/backend.

findings.topic: Cache keys: model_from_cache keyed by integer PK
findings.finding: Cacheable read specs are cached in Redis under 'app.Model:pk:SpecName' with no tenant component. Facility, PatientIdentifierConfig and TagConfig are cacheable (use_base_manager=True for the first two) and are looked up by integer id. Invalidation (post_save delete_pattern) only clears the current schema's id.
findings.evidence: care/emr/resources/base.py:205-213 (model_cache_key), :255-273 (get/set by pk), :293-297 and :313-315 (invalidation by instance.id/external_id); @cacheable at care/emr/resources/facility/spec.py:36, care/emr/resources/patient_identifier/spec.py:78, care/emr/resources/tag/config_spec.py:161, care/emr/resources/user/spec.py:107. Callers by integer id: care/emr/resources/scheduling/slot/spec.py:130 (facility), care/emr/models/patient.py:215,229 (PatientIdentifierListSpec id=x.id), care/emr/tagging/base.py:102 (TagConfigReadSpec id=tag), care/emr/resources/tag/cache_invalidation.py:27-31
findings.tenancy_impact: Each schema has its own sequence (BigAutoField, config/settings/base.py:75), so hospital A Facility id=1 and hospital B Facility id=1 map to the same key. Hospital B can be served hospital A's facility name/address, patient-identifier config or tag definitions, which is a cross-tenant PHI/config leak. UserSpec is safe only if User stays in a single shared schema. Fix with a schema-aware cache KEY_FUNCTION, or by adding the tenant schema to model_cache_key (small logged edit).

findings.finding: BasePatientIdentifierConfig keeps a class-level dict of PatientIdentifierConfig model instances keyed by 'facility.id:system' (or ':system' when there is no facility). It lives for the whole worker process and is never invalidated. update_identifier then creates PatientIdentifier rows with config=<cached instance>. MAINTAIN_FACILITY_PATIENT_NAME_IDENTIFIER defaults to True, so this runs on every Encounter and TokenBooking save.
findings.evidence: care/emr/signals/patient/base.py:17,23-39,68-79; care/emr/signals/patient/facility_name_identifier.py:17,27-46; name_identifier.py:16,26-29; phone_number_identifier.py:16,26-29; default ON at config/settings/config.py:261-263
findings.tenancy_impact: After a gunicorn/celery process serves hospital A, a save in hospital B with the same facility.id (or facility=None) reuses A's PatientIdentifierConfig object. B's PatientIdentifier row then points at A's config_id: either a foreign-key violation, or a silent link to an unrelated config in B's schema. This is a data-corruption bug. The dict must be keyed by schema or removed (logged patch), even if a cache KEY_FUNCTION is added.

findings.finding: FacilityConfig caches computed monetary components and the discount configuration under 'facility:{facility_id}:...' with no timeout. It is invalidated only on save in the current schema.
findings.tenancy_impact: Hospital B's facility id=1 can bill with hospital A's tax and discount components (wrong GST and discounts on invoices). This is a billing-correctness and confidentiality issue. Needs tenant-namespaced keys.

findings.topic: Cache keys: facility and user feature flags
findings.finding: BaseFlag caches flag existence and the list of all flags per entity integer id for one day.
findings.evidence: care/utils/models/base.py:35,49-57,72-92; FacilityFlag keys care/facility/models/facility_flag.py:16-17; UserFlag keys care/users/models.py:244-245
findings.tenancy_impact: Facility flags leak or toggle features across hospitals that share a facility id. This matters if flags are used for per-tenant feature or plugin enablement. User flags are safe only if User is global in a shared schema.

findings.finding: Role permission lists and slug lists are cached for 7 days under 'role_permissions:{role.id}' and 'role_permissions_cache:{role.id}'. They are invalidated by a RolePermission post_save/post_delete receiver in the current schema only.
findings.tenancy_impact: If RoleModel/RolePermission live in each tenant schema (needed for hospital-defined custom roles), role ids collide and a role in B can resolve to A's permission set: privilege escalation or denial. If roles live in a shared schema the keys are safe, but custom roles then become visible to every tenant. Decide where roles live, then namespace the keys.

findings.finding: PlugConfigViewset list/retrieve need no authentication or permission. The list is cached forever under the fixed key 'care_plug_viewset_list'.
findings.tenancy_impact: Whichever tenant fills the cache first, its plugin configuration (which may include integration endpoints and settings) is served unauthenticated to every hospital's subdomain. That is both a leak and a functional bug. Needs a tenant-namespaced key, and plugin config split into global vs per-tenant.

findings.topic: Cache keys: favourites and valueset preferences (incl. raw Redis client)
findings.finding: Favourite-list caches are keyed by user.id + facility.id. Valueset favourites and recent views are keyed by valueset slug + user external_id. RecentViewsManager talks to Redis through get_redis_connection('default') (lrange/lrem/lpush), which bypasses Django cache KEY_PREFIX/KEY_FUNCTION.
findings.tenancy_impact: A doctor working at two hospitals (global user) shares favourite and recent-code caches across both, even though the DB rows are per schema. Cached favourite lists hold integer PKs from the other schema. A cache KEY_FUNCTION fixes the cache.* calls, but RecentViewsManager needs its own patch to prefix keys.

findings.topic: CACHES setting: no key prefix/function; one shared Redis
findings.finding: The default cache is django_redis on REDIS_URL with no KEY_PREFIX, VERSION or KEY_FUNCTION (only the test settings add KEY_PREFIX 'test_'). The same REDIS_URL is also the Celery broker, the result backend and the health-check queue.
findings.tenancy_impact: Every cache, lock and ratelimit key shares one namespace across all hospitals. The cleanest central fix is a KEY_FUNCTION that prepends the current schema name (e.g. django-tenants' make_key), set in our settings and not in CARE code. Keys that should stay global (fhir_resource terminology cache, JWT invalidation by raw token, login ratelimit by username) still work when prefixed. django_redis delete_pattern applies key_func, so pattern invalidation keeps working.

findings.topic: Redis locks: global and integer-keyed lock keys
findings.finding: care.utils.lock.Lock uses 'lock:{key}' in the shared cache. Global singletons: 'lock:create_patient' and 'lock:create_invoice'. Integer-keyed: account, invoice, charge_item, create_facility_encounter:{facility_id}, location/product, booking:resource:{id}, booking:token:{queue.id}, queue:primary/next_token:{id}, facility_location:{id}. OTP locks are keyed by phone number. The sync_permissions_roles lock is global. Inventory and dispense/delivery locks use Postgres SELECT ... FOR UPDATE NOWAIT and are tenant-safe.
findings.evidence: care/utils/lock.py:12-51; care/emr/locks/billing.py:12,18,24,30,36,42; care/emr/locks/inventory.py:8; care/emr/locks/otp.py:8,14; callers care/emr/api/viewsets/patient.py:122, invoice.py:145, encounter.py:193, scheduling/availability.py:127, scheduling/token.py:75, scheduling/token_queue.py:151,186,229, scheduling/schedule.py:170,174,335, location.py:386-402; care/security/management/commands/sync_permissions_roles.py:22; DB-row locks care/emr/locks/billing.py:57-202
findings.tenancy_impact: No data leak, but heavy cross-tenant interference. Patient registration and invoice creation are serialised across all hundreds of hospitals (LOCK_TIMEOUT 32s, base.py:78), and contention returns 'try again' / HTTP 423. Integer-keyed locks give false contention between hospitals with equal ids. Lock.release deletes the key without checking the owner. A schema-aware KEY_FUNCTION fixes all of these centrally.

findings.finding: Tasks found: cleanup_expired_token_slots, cleanup_expired_otps, cleanup_incomplete_file_uploads (periodic); generate_report_task (.delay with template external_id, report_type, associating_id, user_id=int); send_totp_enabled/disabled_email (.delay email, username); summarise_monetary_components (.delay(component.id) recursively for child categories); handle_cascade and rebalance_account_task (decorated @app.task but called synchronously). None takes a schema/tenant argument, and the worker would run on the default search_path.
findings.evidence: care/emr/tasks/__init__.py:12-31; care/emr/tasks/cleanup_expired_token_slots.py:12-21; cleanup_expired_otps.py:14-21; cleanup_incomplete_file_uploads.py:14-57; report_generation.py:12-78 (called care/emr/api/viewsets/report/report_upload.py:147-153 with user_id=request.user.id); totp.py:8-59 (called care/emr/api/viewsets/totp.py:102,139); care/emr/models/resource_category.py:123-140 (sync entry care/emr/api/viewsets/resource_category.py:208); care/emr/models/location.py:9,160-168 (sync call :129); care/emr/resources/account/sync_items.py:14,81-85 (sync calls invoice.py:160..308, payment_reconciliation.py:95..229, charge_item.py:456)
findings.tenancy_impact: generate_report_task and the summarise_monetary_components fan-out would query the wrong schema (public) or fail, and the integer category id is ambiguous without a schema. The three periodic tasks would clean only one schema; they must loop over every tenant (e.g. tenant-schemas-celery or a per-tenant fan-out task). Every .delay needs the tenant schema carried in headers or kwargs, with search_path set in a task_prerun hook. handle_cascade/rebalance work today only because they run in the request thread; turning them into .delay would break them. TOTP emails need no DB but should carry tenant branding.

findings.topic: Celery config: one broker/queue, one beat, IST timezone
findings.finding: Broker and result backend are the same Redis; one default 'celery' queue (watched by the health check); no CELERY_BEAT_SCHEDULER, so beat uses the default file scheduler; the schedule is registered in on_after_finalize; timezone Asia/Kolkata; soft limit 1800s, hard limit 9000s.
findings.tenancy_impact: One hospital's heavy jobs (reports, fan-outs) delay every other hospital: a noisy neighbour. Hundreds of tenants × periodic tasks need batching. Consider per-tenant routing/priority or rate limits, and run a single beat instance. The healthy_django queue-length check only sees the 'celery' queue.

findings.topic: JWT auth (SimpleJWT) not bound to tenant
findings.finding: REST auth order: CustomJWTAuthentication (SimpleJWT, signed with SECRET_KEY since there is no SIGNING_KEY, no audience/issuer, USER_ID_FIELD=external_id), CustomBasicAuthentication, SessionAuthentication, TokenAuthentication. Login, refresh, verify and logout are CARE's own views. Logout invalidation is cached by raw token string.
findings.tenancy_impact: A token issued on hospital-a.<domain> is accepted on hospital-b.<domain>, because no tenant claim is checked. With Keycloak this whole chain must be replaced or wrapped: validate the Keycloak JWT and require the Organization claim to match the subdomain tenant. Basic auth is enabled in prod and should be disabled. Token-invalidation keys are globally unique, so they are safe to share.

findings.topic: Patient OTP token and DRF authtoken not tenant-bound
findings.finding: Patient OTP login issues a PatientToken (SECRET_KEY-signed, 1h) whose only claim is phone_number. Patient OTP endpoints then filter Patient by phone_number. Service-account API tokens use rest_framework.authtoken Token rows.
findings.tenancy_impact: An OTP verified at hospital A gives a token that works on hospital B's subdomain for every patient there with the same phone number: cross-tenant PHI access. Add a tenant claim, check it, and keep MobileOTP per tenant. If the authtoken table sits in a shared schema, a service-account key (e.g. analyzer bridge) works against every hospital, so authtoken should be tenant-schema or tenant-checked.

findings.topic: Global superuser/staff and unscoped user listing
findings.finding: is_superuser short-circuits every authorisation helper and many viewsets. UserViewSet.get_queryset returns all non-deleted users to any authenticated user, with email/phone/username filters. Django admin with import_export exposes Patient and Encounter import/export to is_staff users.
findings.tenancy_impact: If User lives in a shared schema (one global login per person), a CARE superuser or staff flag becomes 'super-admin of every hospital', and any clinician can list and search every user of every hospital. Per-tenant admin rights must come from tenant membership (Keycloak Organization role), not the global User flags. UserViewSet must be filtered to users who are members of the current tenant (needs a patch or a plugin override).

findings.finding: The settings list django.contrib auth, contenttypes, sessions, sites (SITE_ID=1, migration sets domain ohc.network), messages, admin; rest_framework.authtoken, djangoql, maintenance_mode, healthy_django, import_export, django.contrib.postgres; local care.security, care.facility, care.users, care.audit_log, care.emr; plus plugin apps from plug_config manager (currently empty). AUTH_USER_MODEL=users.User.
findings.tenancy_impact: A SHARED_APPS/TENANT_APPS split is needed. Suggested: contenttypes, auth, users (User), sessions, sites, admin and authtoken in the shared schema. The emr/facility clinical and billing models in tenant schemas. Decide care.security (roles/permissions) and system valuesets. Cross-schema FKs from tenant tables to the shared users_user are allowed in Postgres. Plugins are global code (URLs api/{plug}/ in config/urls.py:111-112), so per-tenant enablement needs tenant config. maintenance_mode is process-wide (base.py:440, middleware :205), so it is all-or-nothing for every hospital.

findings.finding: One 'default' DB from DATABASE_URL, ATOMIC_REQUESTS=True, and persistent connections (CONN_MAX_AGE 0 in base, 60 in deployment).
findings.tenancy_impact: Schema routing must SET search_path on every request and Celery task. With CONN_MAX_AGE>0 a reused connection keeps the previous tenant's search_path unless it is reset (django-tenants' backend does this). PgBouncer in transaction mode breaks session-level SET search_path; use session pooling or SET LOCAL inside the atomic request.

findings.finding: Order: Security, CORS, WhiteNoise, Session, Locale, Common, CSRF, Authentication, Messages, BrokenLinkEmails, XFrame, MaintenanceMode, AuditLog. Optional RequestTimeLogging is inserted at index 0. DRF auth happens in the views, not middleware.
findings.tenancy_impact: The tenant-resolution middleware (subdomain → schema) must sit near the top: after Security/CORS, before Session/Auth/AuditLog. The subdomain must be checked against the Keycloak Organization claim inside DRF authentication. CORS/CSRF origins are env lists (deployment.py:48-49, base.py:286) and need a wildcard-subdomain regex. ALLOWED_HOSTS defaults to '*' (base.py:44), which should be tightened to the tenant domains.

findings.finding: Global pre_save/post_save/post_delete receivers log 'AUDIT_LOG::request_id|actor|op|model|ID:pk|changes' to stdout. Details: disabled by default (AUDIT_LOG_ENABLED=False); GET requests skip save(); state is thread-local and cleanup() is never called; per-event state is stored on instance._meta.dal, and _meta is shared by all instances of the model class.
findings.tenancy_impact: Log lines carry no tenant/schema, and the integer PK is ambiguous across schemas, which fails CERT-In/NABH traceability. The thread-local is never cleared, so a later write on the same thread can be attributed to an earlier request, possibly another tenant's. Concurrent saves of the same model class race on _meta.dal. The audit log needs a tenant id plus external_id, and a fixed lifecycle (logged patch, or replace with our own audit plugin).

findings.finding: Other receivers: RolePermission cache invalidation, @cacheable delete_model_cache, TagConfig cache invalidation (post_save), and patient identifier maintenance on Patient/Encounter/TokenBooking save. They query through default managers, so they inherit the current search_path.
findings.tenancy_impact: Database writes are tenant-correct once search_path is set. Their cache invalidations use integer-id keys, so they are only correct if the cache keys are tenant-namespaced. The patient-identifier signal also relies on the unsafe in-process dict (see its own finding).

findings.finding:
- sync_permissions_roles: rewrites PermissionModel/RoleModel/RolePermission from code under one global Redis lock and deletes system roles not in code.
- sync_valueset: upserts system ValueSets by slug.
- load_govt_organization_csv: downloads a CSV and get_or_creates govt Organizations (state/district/local body/ward).
- load_fixtures: runs a script that calls sync commands and drives the API through APIClient (host 'testserver'); blocked when IS_PRODUCTION/!DEBUG.
- migrate_facility_organization: no-op.
- generate_jwks: generates the JWKS.
findings.tenancy_impact: Each must run in the right schema. Shared-schema data: run once. Tenant data: run per tenant during provisioning and after every upstream sync (e.g. a tenant_command wrapper). With the global lock, per-tenant runs must be sequential. load_fixtures' APIClient requests use host 'testserver', which the subdomain tenant middleware cannot resolve, so the seed flow needs a tenant host or schema context. Loading the full India govt hierarchy into hundreds of schemas duplicates large data; see the government-organisations finding.

findings.topic: Organisation hierarchy: govt vs team/role orgs in one table
findings.finding: One Organization model holds org_type govt, team, role and product_supplier. Patients and facilities link to govt orgs through geo_organization and organization_cache arrays. Patient listing and permissions are computed from OrganizationUser memberships with no org restriction. OrganizationPublicViewSet is unauthenticated and lists every organisation.
findings.tenancy_impact: Government geography is the same for every hospital and would ideally be shared, but it cannot be split from tenant team/role orgs without a model change. Putting Organization in each tenant schema (and loading the state/district subset each hospital needs) keeps upstream untouched. check_permission_in_organization with orgs=None grants rights from any membership in the schema, which is acceptable only if OrganizationUser is per tenant.

findings.finding:
Several features span facilities on purpose:
- Patient search by phone number or identifier, and search_retrieve (phone + year of birth + 5-char external_id prefix), query the Patient table with no facility scope.
- PATIENT_GLOBAL_EDIT_ACCESS_ENABLED (env, default False) lets any user with write permission in any organisation edit any patient.
- ResourceRequest is built for origin/approving/assigned facilities across geo organisations.
- getallfacilities (public) and FacilitySchedulableUsers (public) list facilities and their users.
findings.tenancy_impact: Under schema-per-tenant these become hospital-only, which is the desired isolation. But continuity for a patient seen at two hospitals, inter-hospital referrals and transfers (ResourceRequest), and any public 'find a hospital' directory then need a cross-tenant mechanism: ABDM/ABHA consent flows, or a shared-schema referral service. PATIENT_GLOBAL_EDIT_ACCESS and the other config.py flags are process-wide env settings and cannot differ per hospital.

findings.evidence: config/settings/config.py:7-341; config/settings/base.py:301-310 (DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL 'Open Healthcare Network', '[Care]' prefix), :393-397 (Care API title), :715-723 (SMS 'Care OTP...')
findings.tenancy_impact: Cannot vary per hospital without code change: GST treatment, rounding and cancellation policy differ by hospital. Needs a tenant-config layer, e.g. FacilityConfig/plugin settings resolved per tenant, with defaults from env. CARE branding strings also go to patients, which conflicts with the no-CARE-branding rule.

findings.topic: Object storage paths and pre-signed URLs
findings.finding: Single bucket per type from env. Object keys are '{file_type}/{internal_name}', where internal_name = uuid4 + unix time, with no tenant prefix. The REPORT bucket is the same bucket as PATIENT. Pre-signed PUT/GET URLs last 1h and go through the external endpoint. Facility cover images and user avatars are stored at 'cover_images|avatars/{external_id}_{hex}', set public-read when BUCKET_HAS_FINE_ACL, and served by CDN or bucket URL. The patient/report bucket clients are built with FACILITY_S3_KEY/SECRET, not FILE_UPLOAD_KEY/SECRET (upstream bug).
findings.evidence: config/settings/base.py:547-570,682-695; care/utils/csp/config.py:27-81 (patient creds :48-50, report :62-64); care/emr/utils/file_manager.py:35-133; care/emr/models/file_upload.py:33,45-49; care/emr/models/report/report_upload.py:34,50-55; care/emr/reports/report_utils.py:102; care/utils/file_uploads/cover_image.py:24-53; care/facility/models/facility.py:211-213; care/users/models.py:204-206
findings.tenancy_impact: Keys will not collide, but nothing separates tenants in storage: no per-tenant IAM or prefix policy, and no simple per-hospital export, DPDP erasure, retention or lifecycle. cleanup_incomplete_file_uploads must run per schema or it deletes nothing (or only one schema's files). Recommend a tenant prefix ('{schema}/{file_type}/...') in S3FilesManager or a per-tenant bucket (logged patch), plus Indian-region buckets. Public-read avatars and covers are visible across tenants by URL.

findings.topic: IDs exposed in URLs and APIs
findings.finding: All viewset lookups use external_id (UUID), slug (questionnaire, valueset, charge_item_definition, product_knowledge, template, resource_category, activity/observation/specimen definitions, permissions, plug_config) or username (users). There are no integer PK path params. Some responses expose integer user ids (observation created_by_id/updated_by_id/data_entered_by_id), and users_cache arrays hold integer user ids.
findings.tenancy_impact: URLs are safe under schema-per-tenant. Slugs are unique only per schema, which is fine. Integer user ids are consistent across tenants only if User is in a shared schema; if users were per tenant, users_cache and created_by ids would diverge for a doctor at two hospitals.

findings.finding: Report progress and lock are stored in cache 'report_generation_lock:{template_type}_{associating_id}' with a 2-min TTL. The task signature carries template external_id, associating_id and the integer user_id.
findings.tenancy_impact: associating_id is a UUID, so collisions are unlikely. The real problem is the Celery task running without a schema (Template.objects.get fails or reads the wrong schema). The integer user_id is safe only with a global User table.

findings.finding: The healthy_django checks cover only the 'default' DB connection, the default cache and the 'celery' queue length. The FHIR terminology query cache uses the 'fhir_resource:{sha256}' key (10s TTL), which holds no tenant data. SNOWSTORM_DEPLOYMENT_URL defaults to a third-party HTTP IP.
findings.tenancy_impact: The health checks say nothing about per-tenant schema health or migration state; add a tenant-aware check. The terminology cache is safe and useful to keep global (exempt it from tenant prefixing if possible). The Snowstorm default is already tracked as P1-T10.

findings.finding: django_ratelimit uses the shared default cache. The login group is 'login-{username}' with the constant key 'ratelimit'. OTP send/verify limits come from counting MobileOTP rows by phone number.
findings.tenancy_impact: The login ratelimit is global per username, which suits one global login. With MobileOTP rows per tenant schema, a single phone number gets OTP_MAX_SENDS_PER_WINDOW per hospital, multiplying SMS cost and brute-force budget across tenants. Consider a global (shared-schema or Redis) OTP throttle.

findings.finding: The API base URL is fixed when the page loads. care.config.ts first looks up window.location.origin in REACT_CARE_URL_MAP, a JSON map compiled into the bundle, and falls back to REACT_CARE_API_URL. An empty REACT_CARE_API_URL is explicitly allowed and means relative, same-origin API calls. Every request is built as `${baseUrl ?? careConfig.apiUrl}${path}`; no route in src sets its own baseUrl. window.CARE_API_URL just copies careConfig.apiUrl for plugins to read. So one bundle can serve any number of tenant subdomains if REACT_CARE_API_URL is empty: each subdomain calls /api/... on itself, and the reverse proxy forwards to Django with the Host header kept, so django-tenants can resolve the schema. REACT_CARE_URL_MAP cannot scale: it is baked in at build time, so every new hospital would need a frontend rebuild.
findings.evidence: care.config.ts:37-39 (map parsed from build-time env), care.config.ts:45-51 (resolveApiUrl: map[window.location.origin] then REACT_CARE_API_URL), care.config.ts:55 (evaluated once at module load); scripts/validate-env.ts:102-104 (empty string means same-origin; URL_MAP keys must be origins); scripts/validate-env.ts:185-190 (one of the two is required); src/Utils/request/query.ts:16 (url = baseUrl ?? careConfig.apiUrl); src/Utils/request/types.ts:12 (optional per-route baseUrl, unused); src/index.tsx:25 (window.CARE_API_URL = careConfig.apiUrl); deploy/frontend.env:3 (REACT_CARE_API_URL set per build); deploy/docker/frontend-nginx.conf.template:4 and :17 (CSP assumes a separate API origin such as https://api.example.in in connect-src)
findings.tenancy_impact: Decision needed: use same-origin API (REACT_CARE_API_URL="") with the ingress forwarding <tenant>.app.example.in/api/* to Django and keeping Host, so the schema comes from the subdomain. Do not use REACT_CARE_URL_MAP: it needs a rebuild per tenant. A shared api.example.in origin would hide the tenant from Host, so the backend would need a tenant header or a token claim instead. The current CSP template (CSP_API_ORIGIN) assumes that separate API origin and should become connect-src 'self' for API calls. No upstream code change is needed, only build env and ingress.

findings.finding: Staff JWTs are kept in localStorage as care_access_token and care_refresh_token. The patient OTP token is kept as care_patient_token, and the MFA temporary token as mfa_temp_token. Every request reads the access token from localStorage and sends it as an Authorization: Bearer header. Cookies are not used for auth, and fetch never sets credentials. localStorage is scoped to one origin (scheme, host and port), so apollo-nagpur.app.example.in cannot read tokens stored by another hospital's subdomain. The browser keeps tokens apart only by origin; the backend does not. If every tenant shares one SimpleJWT signing key and the user table is global, a token issued on tenant A would also be accepted on tenant B's subdomain unless the backend binds tokens to a tenant. The only cookie set is the sidebar UI cookie. It is host-only (no Domain attribute) and contains no secrets. Any XSS can read localStorage tokens; CSP is the main mitigation.
findings.evidence: src/common/constants.tsx:6-9 (key names); src/Providers/AuthUserProvider.tsx:47-49, 89-90, 99, 114-115, 131-132, 141-144 (writes to localStorage); src/Utils/request/utils.ts:77-82 (Bearer token from localStorage); src/Providers/AuthUserProvider.tsx:148-173 (signOut calls backend logout, then removes keys); src/Providers/AuthUserProvider.tsx:176-196 (storage-event sign-out between tabs of the same origin only); src/Providers/AuthUserProvider.tsx:220-239 (redirect limited to same origin); src/components/ui/sidebar.tsx:90 (cookie with path=/ and no domain); src/atoms/user-atom.ts:5-8 (current user cached in sessionStorage 'care-auth-user')
findings.tenancy_impact: Browser-side isolation is enough if each tenant has its own subdomain origin; never serve two tenants on one origin. On the backend, bind every access and refresh token to the tenant, for example a tenant/org claim checked by middleware against the Host-resolved schema, or a per-tenant signing key. Otherwise a token works on another tenant's subdomain wherever that user also exists. With Keycloak, the org claim plays this role. Keep a strict CSP, because tokens in localStorage can be read by XSS.

findings.topic: Facility selection and doctor working at two hospitals
findings.finding: After login, the user lands on UserDashboard at '/'. It lists user.facilities and user.organizations from the current-user API, plus a responsibilities list. Choosing a facility opens /facility/:id/overview. The sidebar FacilitySwitcher only switches between user.facilities at the same origin. Nothing in the UI knows about tenants: it assumes one API holds all of a user's facilities. A doctor at two hospitals sees only the current subdomain's facilities. Moving to the other hospital means opening a different origin, with its own login and token storage, unless Keycloak SSO signs them in silently. Superuser UI (admin dashboard, /admin/* routes, all permissions) is controlled only by user.is_superuser from the current-user response.
findings.evidence: src/Routers/AppRouter.tsx:75 ('/' renders UserDashboard); src/pages/UserDashboard.tsx:53-76 (facilities, organizations, govt governance, responsibilities); src/pages/UserDashboard.tsx:119 (is_superuser shows admin dashboard); src/components/ui/sidebar/app-sidebar.tsx:100-108, 135-140 (FacilitySwitcher fed by user.facilities); src/components/ui/sidebar/facility/facility-switcher.tsx:112 (href /facility/{id}/overview, same origin); src/types/user/user.ts:56 (facilities: FacilityBareMinimum[]); src/Routers/AppRouter.tsx:141 and src/context/PermissionContext.tsx:38 (isSuperAdmin grants every permission)
findings.tenancy_impact: The backend must build user.facilities and organizations from the current tenant schema only. If the user table is shared in the public schema, a global is_superuser would show platform-admin UI on every hospital's subdomain. Keep superuser for platform staff only and use per-tenant roles for hospital admins. A switcher between hospitals has to be a new ihr_* plugin component that links to other subdomains, ideally with Keycloak SSO. Upstream's FacilitySwitcher cannot do this.

findings.topic: Plugin config (plug_config) and runtime code loading
findings.finding: Before the first render, initI18n calls GET /api/v1/plug_config/, tolerating failure, to find i18n namespaces. PluginEngine calls it again as the 'enabled-plugins' query, and it is invalidated on login. Configs from the API are merged with build-time REACT_ENABLED_APPS. For each config, meta.url is registered as a module-federation remote and its JavaScript is loaded into the app origin. Plugin locales are fetched from the origin in meta.url. Superusers can edit configs in the UI at /admin/apps. The config is read at runtime and depends on Host, so each tenant could enable different plugins without a rebuild. But anyone who can write plug_config can run arbitrary JavaScript on that tenant's origin, which means they can steal tokens.
findings.evidence: src/types/plugConfig/plugConfigApi.ts:12 (GET /api/v1/plug_config/); src/i18n.ts:52-73 (fetched before render, used for namespaces); src/index.tsx:50-57 (initI18n before initApp); src/PluginEngine.tsx:73-79 (enabled-plugins query, 401/403 silent); src/PluginEngine.tsx:39-54 (meta.url becomes a federation remote, ESM loaded at runtime); src/PluginEngine.tsx:115-116 (window.__CARE_PLUGIN_RUNTIME__ meta); src/Utils/plugConfig.ts:12-36, 38-60 (build-time configs override API configs); src/i18n.ts:39-45 (locale fetched from plugin origin); src/Routers/routes/adminRoutes.tsx:42-43 (/admin/apps editor); deploy/docker/frontend-nginx.conf.template:17 (script-src 'self' blocks cross-origin remotes)
findings.tenancy_impact: Decide where plug_config lives. Either in the public schema and editable only by platform operators, or per tenant but read-only to hospital admins. Never let a hospital admin set meta.url. Serve our ihr_* plugin bundles same-origin (for example /plugins/ihr_x/) so that script-src 'self' still holds. Enabling plugins per tenant does work at runtime without a rebuild.

findings.finding: Almost all branding is fixed at build time. The page title, og tags and site name come from %REACT_APP_TITLE% and %REACT_PUBLIC_URL% substituted into index.html. Logos come from the REACT_MAIN_LOGO, REACT_STATE_LOGO, REACT_CUSTOM_LOGO and REACT_CUSTOM_LOGO_ALT JSON. The login description is compiled in through Vite define as __CUSTOM_DESCRIPTION_HTML__. Some strings say 'Care' in the code itself: the PWA manifest name and short_name, the apple-mobile-web-app-title, document.title ' | Care', and the push notification title 'Care - Open Health Care Network'. However, logo values are just URLs used in img src. If they are set to same-origin paths such as /branding/logo.svg, the ingress can serve a different file per Host, which gives per-hospital logos from one bundle.
findings.evidence: index.html:9-18 (%REACT_APP_TITLE%, %REACT_PUBLIC_URL%, %REACT_APP_COVER_IMAGE%); index.html:23 (apple title 'Care'); care.config.ts:59-66 (logos from env JSON); vite.config.mts:422-425 (__CUSTOM_DESCRIPTION_HTML__ define); vite.config.mts:468-470 (manifest name/short_name 'Care'); src/components/Common/PageHeadTitle.tsx:11-13 (' | Care'); src/components/Common/PinPageDialog.tsx:55 (strips ' | CARE'); src/service-worker.ts:36 (notification title); src/components/Auth/AuthHero.tsx:6-38 and src/pages/Landing/LandingPage.tsx:35,160-173 (logos); src/Routers/AppRouter.tsx:162 and src/CAREUI/misc/PrintPreview.tsx:294 (mainLogo on printouts); scripts/validate-env.ts:107-109 (PUBLIC_URL and cover image must be absolute URLs)
findings.tenancy_impact: Per-hospital branding needs a runtime approach. Point logo env values at same-origin paths served per Host, or add an ihr_* branding plugin or override that reads a tenant branding endpoint. The product name and title should be IndieHR or neutral; per-hospital document titles would need a small logged patch or override. The hard-coded 'Care' strings in the manifest, PageHeadTitle and the service-worker notification conflict with the rule not to use 'CARE' in product branding, so they need logged patches (UPSTREAM_PATCHES.md). og:url and the cover image point to one host, which matters little for an authenticated app.

findings.finding: Core translations are loaded from the same origin at /locale/{lng}.json with cache no-store. They can optionally be merged with remote translations from REACT_CUSTOM_REMOTE_I18N_URL, set at build time. Plugin namespaces come from plug_config. The language list includes hi, and REACT_ALLOWED_LOCALES limits the selector; our build sets en,hi. The chosen language is stored in localStorage i18nextLng, separately for each origin.
findings.evidence: src/i18n.ts:13-20 (LANGUAGES incl. hi); src/i18n.ts:80-126 (remote plus local merge); src/i18n.ts:128-151 (plugin namespace URLs); src/i18n.ts:154-165 (init, supportedLngs); care.config.ts i18nUrl = env.REACT_CUSTOM_REMOTE_I18N_URL; src/components/Common/LanguageSelector.tsx:25-26 (localStorage i18nextLng); deploy/frontend.env:12 (REACT_ALLOWED_LOCALES="en,hi")
findings.tenancy_impact: No tenancy risk. One bundle can serve every tenant. Wording or locale overrides per tenant would need a plugin namespace or a same-origin /locale path served per Host. A language preference set on one subdomain does not carry over to another.

findings.topic: Data cached across sessions: TanStack Query persistence
findings.finding: The QueryClient is persisted to localStorage, but only for queries with meta.persist === true: tagConfig (24h staleTime) and productKnowledge. Persisted query keys do not include a tenant. clearQueryPersistenceCache(), called before login, only invalidates these queries, so the persisted data stays in localStorage until it is refetched. On signOut, only ['currentUser'] is reset. The in-memory cache and the FiltersCache entries in localStorage (filters--<pathname>, which can hold patient search terms) survive logout, and are cleared only when the next login is submitted. Persisted data and filters live in per-origin localStorage, so they cannot cross tenant subdomains. They can carry over between users of one tenant on a shared workstation.
findings.evidence: src/Utils/request/queryClient.ts:34-45 (localStorage persister, shouldDehydrateQuery meta.persist, buster from 'app-version'); src/Utils/request/queryClient.ts:47-53 (clear = invalidate only); src/types/emr/tagConfig/useTagConfig.ts:19-28 (key ['tagConfig', id, facilityId], persist); src/components/Questionnaire/ManageResponseTemplatesSheet.tsx:96-101 (productKnowledge persist); src/components/Auth/Login.tsx:243-250 (ViewCache, FiltersCache, practitioner and persistence clears on login submit); src/Providers/AuthUserProvider.tsx:169 (signOut resets only currentUser); src/Utils/FiltersCache.tsx:6-8, 40-46 (filters--pathname in localStorage); src/atoms/queuePractitionerAtom.ts:9-14; src/types/scheduling/schedule.ts:295-301 ('user' in localStorage, public appointments); src/atoms/encounterFilterAtom.ts:29-35, 62-67 (sessionStorage)
findings.tenancy_impact: No cross-tenant leak with one origin per tenant, because all keys are origin-scoped. If tenants ever share an origin, for example path-based /t/<tenant>, every one of these caches would collide, so make subdomain-per-tenant a hard rule in the ADR. For shared hospital PCs (DPDP), a small ihr patch or plugin hook should run queryClient.clear(), remove the persisted cache and FiltersCache on signOut.

findings.finding: The service worker uses injectManifest with Workbox precacheAndRoute over build assets only. It has no runtime caching routes, so API responses and PHI are never stored in Cache Storage. It calls clientsClaim and supports skipWaiting. Registration and caches are per origin, so each tenant subdomain installs its own copy of the same precache. Push messages go to clients[0] of that origin only. clearAllCaches(), used on app update, deletes all caches, unregisters service workers and clears the query cache. App version is polled through a build-meta fetch.
findings.evidence: src/service-worker.ts:13 (precacheAndRoute(self.__WB_MANIFEST) only); src/service-worker.ts:15-23 (clientsClaim, SKIP_WAITING); src/service-worker.ts:26-43 (push handling, clients[0]); vite.config.mts:456-467 (VitePWA injectManifest, maximumFileSizeToCacheInBytes 8MB); src/index.tsx:29-31 (registerSW); src/lib/appVersion.ts:86-104 (clearAllCaches)
findings.tenancy_impact: Low risk: there is no data caching and all scope is per origin. The cost is a full precache download on each tenant subdomain a user visits, which is acceptable. If push notifications are ever enabled, the backend must send per-tenant VAPID subscriptions tied to the subdomain origin. Keep runtime API caching out of any future service-worker changes.

findings.topic: Upstream nginx and CSP vs. wildcard subdomains
findings.finding: Upstream's nginx sends HSTS with includeSubDomains and preload, and a Report-Only CSP that lists OHC's S3 buckets. Our deploy template replaces it with an enforcing CSP that has script-src 'self', with connect-src and img-src built from CSP_API_ORIGIN and CSP_STORAGE_ORIGIN at container start. With same-origin APIs, the same image and CSP can serve *.app.example.in. Pre-signed upload URLs come from the backend, and XHR uploads go straight to storage.
findings.evidence: apps/frontend/nginx/nginx.conf:9 and :14 (HSTS preload; report-only CSP with OHC S3); deploy/docker/frontend-nginx.conf.template:4-5, :17 (enforcing CSP variables); deploy/docker/frontend.Dockerfile:10-12 (CSP_API_ORIGIN and CSP_STORAGE_ORIGIN at docker run); src/Utils/request/uploadFile.ts:29 (xhr.open to the given signed URL); vite.config.mts:412-418 (default REACT_CDN_URLS are OHC buckets, preview only)
findings.tenancy_impact: One nginx image can serve every tenant behind a wildcard certificate. CSP_STORAGE_ORIGIN must be one shared object-storage origin, or a wildcard. The backend must still issue pre-signed URLs only for the tenant's own bucket or prefix. HSTS preload on the parent domain is only safe once every subdomain is HTTPS.

frontend.summary: Read-only review of apps/frontend; no files were modified. A single CARE frontend build can serve many hospitals by subdomain, provided the build sets REACT_CARE_API_URL="" (validate-env.ts:102 allows an empty value, meaning same-origin API calls; query.ts:16 builds every URL from careConfig.apiUrl) and the ingress forwards <tenant>.app.example.in/api/* to Django with Host preserved. REACT_CARE_URL_MAP is a build-time JSON map (care.config.ts:37-51), so it would need a rebuild for each new tenant, and our CSP template currently assumes a separate API origin (frontend-nginx.conf.template:4,17). Auth uses JWTs in localStorage (constants.tsx:6-9, AuthUserProvider.tsx:89-132, utils.ts:77-82), sent as a Bearer header with no auth cookies. Since localStorage is per origin, tokens and every cache (persisted TanStack queries, FiltersCache, practitioner and user atoms) are isolated between tenant subdomains, so subdomain-per-tenant must be a hard rule; the browser cannot stop a token issued on one tenant from being accepted on another, so the backend must bind tokens to a tenant (claim or key). Facility selection (UserDashboard.tsx:53, facility-switcher.tsx:112) assumes one API per user. A doctor at two hospitals needs a cross-subdomain switcher in an ihr_* plugin plus Keycloak SSO, and a global is_superuser would grant admin UI on every tenant (AppRouter.tsx:141). plug_config is fetched at runtime (i18n.ts:55, PluginEngine.tsx:73), and its meta.url loads remote JavaScript (PluginEngine.tsx:46-54), so it must be writable only by platform operators, with plugins served same-origin under script-src 'self'. Branding is mostly build-time (index.html:9, care.config.ts:59-66, vite.config.mts:422-470), and 'Care' is hard-coded in several places (PageHeadTitle.tsx:11, service-worker.ts:36, manifest). Per-hospital logos can work without a rebuild if they point at same-origin paths served per Host. i18n is runtime and same-origin, so it is fine. The service worker precaches static assets only, with no API caching (service-worker.ts:13). On a shared workstation, signOut leaves the in-memory query cache and FiltersCache in place (AuthUserProvider.tsx:169); this is a risk within one tenant only.

research.summary: P1-T0 research (2026-11-05). django-tenants 4.0.1 (23 Oct 2026) supports Django 5.2, 6.0 and 6.1 and works with CARE's stack. Its CI tests Postgres 14-17 by name and Postgres 18 only through the postgres:latest image. It has two hard limits. First, it sets search_path per session, which leaks between tenants under PgBouncer transaction pooling (issue #1112 is open), so we need session pooling. Second, 4.0.0 and earlier have a schema-name SQL injection, so we must pin 4.0.1 or later. tenant-schemas-celery 5.0.0 (1 Aug 2026) handles Celery: it tags each task with the schema in a `_schema_name` header, and its tenant-aware beat runs a schedule entry on every tenant unless the entry lists schemas. If a task has no header it runs in public, so every task CARE sends must use TenantTask. django-pgschemas 1.3.2 (6 Sep 2026) is active and adds routing by session or header, but it is the smaller project. RLS would mean editing every CARE model, which conflicts with ADR-002 and the goal of keeping upstream untouched. Biggest tenancy finding: a global login means CARE's `users` app must be a shared app, but `users.User` has FKs to tenant tables (`home_facility` points to facility.Facility and `geo_organization` points to emr.Organization). That breaks the rule that shared models must not FK into tenant models, so it needs a small logged edit (Q-S1). Next: CARE's simplejwt tokens are signed with one SECRET_KEY and carry no tenant, audience or issuer, so a token from tenant A is accepted on tenant B. We need a tenant claim checked by a custom auth class, or Keycloak tokens checked against the organization claim. Keycloak 26.8.x (26.8.2 came out today) puts membership in an `organization` claim keyed by alias, and the client can ask for `organization:<alias>` scope. Keycloak matches an organization by the user's email domain, not by our subdomain, so the backend must check the claim against request.tenant. In NHA's official ABDM wrapper, the gateway sends X-HIP-ID on incoming HIP requests, so a public-schema map from HIP/HFR id to tenant can route them. Replies (on-*) only carry the requestId we sent, so we also need a public-schema map from requestId to tenant. The official ABDM v3 header list was not available; this is inferred from NHA wrapper code and should be confirmed in the sandbox. Sources were read in local clones in the scratchpad, under /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ubuntu-AI-Projects-IndieHR/64868586-0b5d-45fd-9ee5-0f1462c7bad4/scratchpad/ (subfolders dt/src, tsc, abdmw, kc), plus CARE files in /home/ubuntu/AI Projects/IndieHR/apps/backend/config/settings/base.py and /home/ubuntu/AI Projects/IndieHR/apps/backend/care/users/models.py.

findings.finding: Latest is django-tenants 4.0.1, released 2026-10-23; 4.0.0 came out 2026-10-09 and 3.14.0 on 2026-08-05. It declares Django 5.2, 6.0 and 6.1 and Python 3.10 or newer (Django 6.1 itself needs Python 3.12+). Django 6.1 support came in 3.14.0, which fixed an import cycle that had stopped manage.py from starting. Version 4.0.1 is a security release: schema names were not escaped in SET search_path, CREATE SCHEMA and DROP SCHEMA, allowing SQL injection (GHSA-693j-7v9f-x7pw), and versions 3.4.8 to 4.0.0 are affected. 4.0.0 has breaking changes: subfolder tenants now get a per-tenant URLconf, and schema_exists is case-sensitive. CI tests Postgres 14, 15, 16 and 17 by name; the Django-compatibility jobs use postgres:latest, which is 18 today. Postgres 18 is therefore exercised but not pinned in CI (uncertain).
findings.evidence: https://pypi.org/project/django-tenants/ ; https://github.com/django-tenants/django-tenants/releases (v4.0.1, v4.0.0, v3.14.0 notes read via gh api) ; .github/workflows/code.yml at commit 8f933cfe (matrix postgres-version: [14,15,16,17] and [latest]) ; pyproject.toml classifiers
findings.tenancy_impact: It works with CARE's Django 6.1.2 and psycopg 3.3.2. Pin it at 4.0.1 or later. Also validate schema names ourselves: lowercase a-z, digits and underscore, derived from a slug we control and never typed by the user. Add a Postgres 18 job to our own CI rather than relying on upstream's postgres:latest.

findings.finding: django-tenants issues a session-level `SET search_path` (postgresql_backend/base.py, line 217). The 3.14.0 release notes say this "leaks between tenants under transaction pooling" and that only session pooling is safe. Issue #1112 ('Issues with PGBouncer Transaction Mode') is still open as of 2026-07-25. CARE sets CONN_MAX_AGE=0 and ATOMIC_REQUESTS=True. TENANT_LIMIT_SET_CALLS=True sets search_path once per request instead of on every cursor.
findings.tenancy_impact: This is a direct risk of one tenant's data reaching another. Any pooler (PgBouncer, RDS Proxy or a cloud pooler) must use session mode, or we skip pooling and rely on Django persistent connections. Record this in the ADR, and add a test asserting that `SHOW search_path` matches request.tenant on pooled connections. At hundreds of tenants, connection counts are limited by session pooling, not by the number of schemas.

findings.topic: SHARED_APPS / TENANT_APPS, FK rule, CARE's User model
findings.finding: Apps in SHARED_APPS are migrated only into the public schema, and apps in TENANT_APPS only into tenant schemas. Public is always on the search_path, so a tenant table can FK to a shared table. A shared table cannot FK to a tenant table, because the referenced table does not exist in public. This is inferred from the routing design and community threads; the current docs do not state it outright. The docs also warn that moving an app between the two lists later needs `migrate --fake zero` steps. In CARE, `users.User` (AUTH_USER_MODEL) has FKs to tenant tables: `home_facility` points to facility.Facility (PROTECT) and `geo_organization` points to emr.Organization. UserSkill and UserFlag point back to User. CARE's apps include contrib.admin (LogEntry has FKs to User and ContentType), rest_framework.authtoken, and contenttypes, which care/emr/utils/file_manager.py and care/emr/reports/report_utils.py use.
findings.evidence: https://django-tenants.readthedocs.io/en/latest/install.html (SHARED_APPS/TENANT_APPS, 'Moving apps between' warning) ; https://github.com/bcarneiro/django-tenant-schemas/issues/43 ; https://github.com/django-tenants/django-tenants/issues/962 (open: deleting shared record with FK from tenant) ; local: apps/backend/care/users/models.py lines 117-145, config/settings/base.py lines 112-139
findings.tenancy_impact: A global login (ADR-002, one person across hospitals) means `care.users`, auth and sessions are SHARED. Then User.home_facility and User.geo_organization are shared-to-tenant FKs and cannot work as real FKs. We need a minimal logged edit (Q-S1): make them nullable with db_constraint=False and never cross-schema joined, or move them to a per-tenant 'staff profile' row in an ihr_* plugin. Put contenttypes in BOTH lists so ContentType ids are consistent inside each schema, and never store ContentType ids across schemas. Deleting a shared User while tenant tables still reference it hits issue #962, so prefer soft-delete or deactivation. CARE's tenant-side created_by/updated_by FKs to User point from tenant to shared and are fine.

findings.finding: The django-tenants security doc requires auth and sessions to sit at the same level. Auth in TENANT_APPS with sessions in SHARED_APPS lets one tenant impersonate another (issue #52). With global accounts in SHARED_APPS, the doc warns that the setup 'is a cross-tenant access bug unless you restrict which tenants a user may enter'. It recommends middleware after AuthenticationMiddleware that checks a user-to-request.tenant relation and returns 403. Cache-backed sessions need a tenant-aware KEY_FUNCTION.
findings.tenancy_impact: We need a mandatory TenantMembershipMiddleware (or a DRF permission) that checks the user's membership in request.tenant. Membership comes from a public-schema membership table or the Keycloak organization claim, and the check covers JWT, Basic and Session auth alike. CARE enables CustomBasicAuthentication and SessionAuthentication besides JWT, and each needs the same check. Consider disabling Basic auth in production.

findings.finding: TENANT_MODEL (a subclass of TenantMixin) and TENANT_DOMAIN_MODEL (a subclass of DomainMixin) must be in a SHARED app that also includes 'django_tenants'. The DB engine is django_tenants.postgresql_backend, and the router is django_tenants.routers.TenantSyncRouter. TenantMainMiddleware goes at the top of MIDDLEWARE and resolves the tenant from the Host header. PUBLIC_SCHEMA_URLCONF serves the public schema. A 'public' tenant row must exist. Domain names and schema names follow different rules: hyphens are allowed in domains but not schemas, and underscores the other way round. For local dev, `*.localhost` subdomains work.
findings.evidence: https://django-tenants.readthedocs.io/en/latest/install.html ; docs/index.rst warning on schema vs domain names ; https://django-tenants.readthedocs.io/en/latest/use.html ('Running in Development')
findings.tenancy_impact: Create an ihr_tenancy plugin app holding Hospital(TenantMixin) and Domain(DomainMixin). Add a separate schema_name generator, for example `h_<shortid>`, kept apart from the subdomain slug. The ALLOWED_HOSTS and CSRF and CORS origins must accept `*.<product-domain>`. The frontend's API origin becomes per-tenant, and the nginx CSP_API_ORIGIN must allow a wildcard subdomain.

findings.topic: migrate_schemas executors at hundreds of schemas
findings.finding: There are three executors: standard (serial), multiprocessing (TENANT_MULTIPROCESSING_MAX_PROCESSES, default 2, and TENANT_MULTIPROCESSING_CHUNKS) and subprocess, added in 3.12.0. Subprocess starts a fresh `migrate_schemas --schema X` per tenant, with --parallel N or TENANT_SUBPROCESS_PARALLEL. The docs say it exists because the in-process runner never frees memory across tenants 'until the OOM killer reaps the process'. The first non-zero exit stops the run, and in-flight DDL is allowed to finish. TENANT_CREATION_FAKES_MIGRATIONS with BASE_SCHEMA creates a new tenant by cloning a template schema instead of running migrations. I found no official benchmark at hundreds of schemas. A community article says catalog bloat (pg_class and pg_attribute) slows DDL at around 2,000 schemas of 50 tables each, without numbers (anecdotal).
findings.tenancy_impact: CARE has many models (60+ emr modules) and a large migration graph, so each upstream sync multiplies migration time by the tenant count. Use `--executor=subprocess --parallel N` in deploy jobs, and use a template schema for fast onboarding. Run a P1 spike: time migrations for 1 versus 50 schemas, and measure catalog size, before committing to hundreds of tenants per cluster. Unverified: cost at more than 500 schemas times CARE's table count.

findings.finding: Setting CACHES['default'] KEY_FUNCTION='django_tenants.cache.make_key' prefixes keys with connection.schema_name, giving keys of the form schema:prefix:version:key. django-redis also needs REVERSE_KEY_FUNCTION='django_tenants.cache.reverse_key'. CARE uses django-redis 6.0.0 with IGNORE_EXCEPTIONS and a separate locmem 'swagger_cache'.
findings.tenancy_impact: Add both functions to CARE's default cache, a settings-only change outside apps/. Celery tasks and any raw redis-py use (redis.Redis or cache.client direct calls) bypass KEY_FUNCTION, so audit CARE for direct Redis calls and give them a tenant prefix. Rate limiting (django_ratelimit) keys go through the cache, so they will become per-tenant, which is acceptable.

findings.finding: django-tenants ships only TenantFileSystemStorage (local disk, MULTITENANT_RELATIVE_MEDIA_ROOT with '%s' set to schema_name), now configured through STORAGES, plus TenantStaticFilesStorage. It has no S3 backend. CARE stores files in S3-compatible buckets (FILE_UPLOAD_BUCKET, FACILITY_S3_BUCKET via boto3 and BUCKET_PROVIDER), not in Django's default storage.
findings.tenancy_impact: django-tenants storage does not help here. We need an ihr_* wrapper so that CARE's file_manager writes keys under `<schema_or_tenant_uuid>/...`, or a bucket per tenant, kept in Indian regions. Signed URLs must be generated only for keys in the current tenant's prefix. This probably means a logged edit to care/emr/utils/file_manager.py.

findings.finding: django-pgschemas 1.3.2 was uploaded 2026-09-06. It requires Python 3.12 or newer and declares Django 5.2, 6.0 and 6.1. Its repo was pushed 2026-11-05, has 161 stars, 0 open issues and is not archived; one maintainer (lorinkoz) leads it. It is a fork of django-tenants with static tenants that can have their own apps and urlconf, plus dynamic tenants. It routes by subdomain, subfolder, session or request header. It runs management commands across schemas, in parallel through threads, and discourages relying on overriding the public schema. Compared with django-tenants (1,899 stars, 93 open issues, releases in 2026-10), its community is much smaller and tenant-schemas-celery does not officially target it. Its README is written for django-tenants.
findings.evidence: https://pypi.org/pypi/django-pgschemas/json ; https://github.com/lorinkoz/django-pgschemas ; gh api repos/lorinkoz/django-pgschemas and repos/django-tenants/django-tenants (stats on 2026-11-05)
findings.tenancy_impact: Header routing would suit the ABDM bridge and internal calls, but django-tenants plus a small custom middleware does the same. Keep django-tenants as the default because of its larger community and Celery integration. Treat pgschemas as a fallback. Also check whether pgschemas has the same session-level SET search_path (not checked).

findings.topic: Alternatives: custom search_path middleware and Postgres RLS
findings.finding: A thin custom middleware that runs `SET search_path` per request repeats about 30% of django-tenants: per-schema migrations, the sync router, tenant creation and cloning. It carries the same transaction-pooling hazard unless it uses `SET LOCAL` inside ATOMIC_REQUESTS, and CARE has ATOMIC_REQUESTS=True. Postgres RLS (shared schema plus a tenant_id column and policies) needs a tenant_id on every CARE table, an edit to every upstream model, and the app must connect as a non-owner, non-BYPASSRLS role or use FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. The Postgres docs say superusers, BYPASSRLS roles and, by default, table owners bypass policies.
findings.tenancy_impact: RLS conflicts with ADR-002 and with keeping upstream untouched, because every CARE model would gain a tenant_id. Rejected unless ADR-002 is revisited. Fixing #1112 upstream with an opt-in `SET LOCAL` mode under ATOMIC_REQUESTS would be a valuable contribution, but it is not a reason to fork. Record both alternatives in the ADR as considered and rejected.

findings.finding: tenant-schemas-celery 5.0.0 was released 2026-08-01; 4.0.3 came out 2025-08-01. It requires Python 3.11 or newer and celery>=5. Its CI matrix tests Celery latest, <5.5 and <5.4 against Django latest and <6, with django-tenants. Django is not pinned, so 6.1 is covered by testing against 'latest' rather than by a classifier. The repo was pushed 2026-11-03. The README says the schema travels in task kwargs, but that is out of date: the code adds a `_schema_name` message header (task.py, headers_with_schema). The worker's task_prerun handler switches the connection with set_tenant(include_public=True), and **a task with no header runs in the public schema**. Use `CeleryApp` from tenant_schemas_celery.app, and set TASK_TENANT_CACHE_SECONDS to cache tenant lookups.
findings.tenancy_impact: CARE's Celery app must become the TenantAwareCeleryApp, and every CARE `@shared_task` must use the tenant-aware task base. Otherwise tasks sent from a tenant request silently run in public and fail or, worse, write shared data. Add a test that sends each CARE task from inside tenant_context and asserts the schema. CARE is on Celery 5.6.0, which is newer than the 'latest' this CI pins, so verify it in our CI.

findings.finding: CARE registers its beat tasks in code (`on_after_finalize`, `add_periodic_task` in care/emr/tasks/__init__.py, two daily crontabs plus one conditional). tenant-schemas-celery's TenantAwareScheduler and TenantAwarePersistentScheduler run each beat entry on every non-public tenant by default (the `_all_tenants_only` header), or only on the schemas named in the entry's `tenant_schemas` list, for example ['public']. Overriding get_queryset() limits which tenants run, for example only active ones. TenantAwareDatabaseScheduler is for django-celery-beat and needs task names unique across schemas (`name@schema`). The README warns of a 'thundering herd', since all tenants are scheduled at once, and of migrations racing with beat.
findings.tenancy_impact: Use TenantAwarePersistentScheduler with get_queryset filtered to active tenants whose migrations are complete. Spread midnight IST jobs across tenants with jitter, or use a dispatcher task with rate limits. Mark platform-wide jobs with tenant_schemas=['public']. Check whether add_periodic_task entries pass through the tenant-aware conversion (_tenant_aware_beat_schedule_to_dict reads app.conf.beat_schedule). Unverified: CARE's code-registered entries may need moving into beat_schedule.

findings.finding: CARE uses djangorestframework-simplejwt 5.5.1, released 2025-07-21. That is still the latest release, and its classifiers stop at Django 5.2, though CARE runs it on 6.1.2. CARE's SIMPLE_JWT has no AUDIENCE, ISSUER or SIGNING_KEY override, so it uses HS256 with SECRET_KEY. Its auth class is config.authentication.CustomJWTAuthentication, alongside CustomBasicAuthentication and SessionAuthentication. In simplejwt, AUDIENCE and ISSUER are single fixed settings with no per-request or dynamic audience. A token minted on hospital-a.<domain> therefore validates on hospital-b.<domain>, because the key is the same and the user is global (shared). django-tenants issue #955 notes simplejwt blacklist problems under tenancy.
findings.tenancy_impact: This is a cross-tenant replay. Fix in a plugin plus a small logged edit to config/authentication.py: add a `tid` (tenant UUID) claim when issuing tokens (custom token class), and in CustomJWTAuthentication reject any token whose tid differs from request.tenant. Optionally use a per-tenant derived HMAC key (HKDF(SECRET_KEY, tenant_uuid)), which needs a custom TokenBackend. If Keycloak becomes the only token issuer, validate RS256 against JWKS and check `aud` equals our client and `organization` contains request.tenant's alias or id. The membership middleware must also cover Basic and Session auth.

findings.topic: Keycloak 26.8 Organizations claim and one-realm multi-tenancy
findings.finding: Keycloak 26.8.2 was released 2026-11-05 (26.8.1 on 2026-10-13). The docs say Organizations 'enables multi-tenancy within a realm'. The client asks for the built-in optional `organization` client scope, and its 'Organization Membership' mapper emits `"organization": {"<alias>": {"id": ..., attrs}}`. id and attributes are off by default and must be enabled in the mapper. Scope forms: `organization` gives one org, or prompts the user to choose if they belong to several. `organization:<alias>` gives that org, and the request is rejected if the user is not a member. `organization:*` gives all of the user's orgs. Mixing forms is an error. A user can be an unmanaged member of several orgs, which covers a doctor at two hospitals. Domains (including `*.` wildcards) match a user's EMAIL domain during identity-first login, can redirect to an org's identity provider, and appear as a `domain` claim. They do not map the request hostname. Once any org exists, identity-first login becomes the browser-flow default. There is no official limit on organizations per realm. Vendor and community sources cite thousands to 10k+ orgs in one realm and roughly 1 vCPU per 15 password logins per second (anecdotal).
findings.evidence: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/releases (26.8.2 at 2026-11-05) ; docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/organizations/mapping-organization-claims.adoc, intro.adoc, managing-domains.adoc, authenticating-members.adoc, managing-members.adoc @ tag 26.8.2 ; https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/index.html#_managing_organizations ; https://skycloak.io/blog/multi-tenant-authentication-architecture-guide/ (anecdotal) ; https://forum.keycloak.org/t/keycloak-multi-tenancy-extensions-for-saas-applications/15426 (anecdotal)
findings.tenancy_impact: Use one realm and one SPA client. The frontend derives the alias from its subdomain and requests `organization:<alias>`, so Keycloak itself refuses non-members at login. The backend must still check claim key or id against request.tenant on every request, because the realm issuer and audience are shared by all tenants. Bind on the org UUID by enabling 'Add organization id' and storing keycloak_org_id on the Tenant row, not just the alias. Hospital staff mostly use personal email (gmail), so do not depend on email-domain org matching. Since identity-first login becomes the default, the login UX changes. Uncertain: whether an org alias can be renamed after creation; store the UUID to be safe. Load-test the organization claim at 300+ orgs in P1.

findings.topic: ABDM v3 callback routing to tenant
findings.finding: In ABDM v3, an integrator registers one bridge URL per client id (PATCH /api/hiecm/gateway/v3/bridge/url, with X-CM-ID 'sbx' or 'abdm'). Facilities (HIP or HIU services, by HFR id) are attached to that bridge and listed through GET /api/hiecm/gateway/v3/bridge-services. In NHA's official ABDM-wrapper (v3 profile), gateway-initiated HIP requests are routed by the `X-HIP-ID` request header, which the wrapper reads into hipId. Examples are discover (/api/v3/hip/patient/care-context/discover), link init and confirm, consent notify, health-information request and patient share. HIU flows use `X-HIU-ID`. Reply callbacks (on-*, for example /api/v3/link/on_carecontext and /api/v3/hip/token/on-generate-token) are matched by `response.requestId` against the REQUEST-ID we sent, not by a facility header. Requests also carry REQUEST-ID, TIMESTAMP, X-CM-ID and a gateway Authorization JWT. No official public v3 header spec page was retrieved: header names come from NHA wrapper code, last commit 2025-02-21. A forum post shows `X_HIP_ID` with underscores (uncertain).
findings.tenancy_impact: Run a single public-schema ABDM bridge endpoint, not per-subdomain. It verifies the gateway JWT, then resolves the tenant: (a) X-HIP-ID or X-HIU-ID looked up in a public table mapping HFR facility id to tenant (unique constraint; one hospital may have several HFR ids); (b) for on-* replies, a public table mapping outgoing REQUEST-ID or link token to tenant and schema, written when we send. It then runs the handler inside tenant_context or sends a Celery task with that schema. Reject requests where the header and the correlated tenant disagree. Confirm the header names and casing in the ABDM sandbox (P2) before relying on them.
